Subject: Recap + next steps: throughput headroom and fallback model plan for CivicHealth

Thanks for taking the call earlier, Sarah — appreciate the clear context. Quick recap from my side and proposed next steps so we keep momentum.

What we heard (pain & goals)
- Primary goal: real-time clinical triage suggestions in the clinician UI with p95 latency target <= 120ms for short prompts (patient triage snippets) and sustained peak of ~200 QPS during daytime windows.
- Pain: current in-house model is inconsistent under load; spikes cause >500ms tail latency and occasional timeouts.
- Compliance: SOC 2 and US data residency are must-haves; procurement needs standard evidence and a simple MPA.
- Deployment preference: private VPC deployment (AWS us-east) with the option to burst to dedicated pooled capacity for traffic spikes.

Preliminary technical notes (for Rishi / Marissa)
- We recommend a dedicated pool for baseline capacity + burst instances to cover 2.5x traffic spikes. KV prefix caching for common triage prompts will reduce token cost and tail latency.
- Fallback plan: route to smaller distilled model (e.g., 7B quantized) when latency SLOs are in danger; keep higher-capacity model for quality-critical paths.

Attachments: redwood-ops-playbook.pdf (ops runbook + SLOs) attached for reference.

Next steps (action items)
1) Rishi: deep-dive on topology + preliminary sizing and whether int8 quantization fits your model mix (target: by Mon 09/28).
2) Sarah: introduce procurement contact and confirm timeline for contract review; also share any internal eval prompts you want in the QoE evaluation.
3) Tessa/Marissa: we will prepare a short MPA draft and SOC2 link.

Would 30 minutes on Mon (09/28) 10:00am ET work for the topology deep-dive? If that slot doesn't work, suggest an alternative.

Thanks — tessa

Thanks — joining the Monday deep-dive. Quick technical baseline and my ask for the call: 

Topology suggestion (high level)
- Baseline: Private VPC deployment (customer-managed control plane) with a dedicated pool of GPU instances for CivicHealth (pin to us-east region).
- Autoscale policy: keep baseline capacity for 200 QPS steady-state (estimate below) with burst pool able to add ~2.5x additional capacity for 15-30 minute spikes.
- Fallback routing: implement policy that routes non-critical prompts to a distilled 7B quantized variant when p95 > 120ms or error rate climbs above 2%.

Preliminary sizing estimates (very conservative)
- Model: Llama2-13B (float16) for quality-critical paths; distilled 7B int8 for fallback.
- Baseline compute: 4 x GPUs (A100 40GB equiv) in dedicated pool -> approximate steady p95 latency for short prompts: ~80-110ms; throughput ~180-220 QPS depending on batching.
- Burst: +8 smaller GPUs (A10 / T4 class) able to handle additional 350 QPS in aggregate for short windows.

Latency/throughput controls
- Continuous batching with dynamic shard sizing for small prompts (target batch size 8-16 for sub-200ms p95).
- Prefix+KV caching for repeated triage templates — expect 30–45% token savings and improved tail latency.
- Quantization: int8 for fallback will reduce memory pressure and allow denser packing for burst nodes. We'll run benchmark on your sample prompts.

Attached: sizing-estimate.xlsx (worksheet: baseline_vs_burst) and quantization-guide.pdf (summary + caveats).

Questions for CivicHealth on the call
1) Typical prompt length distribution (sample averages you can share).
2) Acceptable QoE thresholds for fallback model (are there endpoints where fallback is never acceptable?).
3) Any integration constraints for VPC peering / egress auditing.

I will bring a short benchmarking plan to validate these numbers during the call.

-Rishi
